items.heading: Heading
items.paragraph:
One last part of responsibility, and one that often gets overlooked, is the responsibility for personal brand. You’ve likely heard the term “personal brand” over the years, whether you’ve given much thought to yours or not.

A personal brand is a unique identity that defines who you are, what you stand for, and how you are perceived by others. It encompasses your personality, values, skills, achievements, and reputation. In today's world, personal branding has become an important aspect of one's professional success. A strong personal brand can help you establish a professional image, increase your credibility, and stand out from the competition.

items.heading: Heading
items.paragraph:
How many times have you heard these words:

(Click on each circle in the illustration below to complete this element)

items.description: “I don’t care what people think of me.”
“If they don’t like me, that’s their fault.”
“Why should I change how I communicate?”
“I’m not here to make friends.”
“I’m just here to get a job done, not make small talk.”

items.heading: Heading
items.paragraph:
You may have even thought some of these yourself! These statements revolve around the concept of personal brand, and the speaker’s willingness (or lack thereof) to change anything about their brand.

You may be tempted to dismiss personal brand, say that it doesn’t matter, or even put the responsibility on others, thinking it’s their job to have a good opinion about you. But the truth is, personal brand is a unique area of responsibility — no one can be responsible for your personal brand but you.

Which of these statements shows mindfulness versus lack of awareness for personal brand?

items.heading: Heading
items.paragraph:
The Legend. The General. The Queen of Rocky Top. The Torchbearer. The Godmother of Women’s Basketball.

Pat herself had a strong personal brand built around her dedication to the sport, her unwavering work ethic, and commitment to excellence both on and off the court. She was known for her toughness, her ability to motivate and inspire her players, and her strong leadership skills. She was also known for her composure, the “Summitt Stare,” and her well-manicured look on the sidelines.

Believe it or not, Pat’s own personal brand went through quite a transformation in a period of just a few short years. Raised on a farm in Henrietta, Tenn., in high school she was known as Trish (short for Patricia) Head. When she went to college, her sorority friends assumed she was Pat, and she didn’t correct them.

“Trish Head was a farm kid with crooked teeth and all the wrong clothes who said ain’t, reckon, and yonder,” Pat recalled. “You never get a second chance to make a first impression. In those early days at college, I realized that presentation counts. For better or worse, strangers made sweeping judgements based on my appearance and demeanor. So, I began the process of self-transformation.”1

image.originalUrl: Summitt on Sideline at Tennessee Tech.1979-80.jpg

items.paragraph:
She quickly enlisted two friends to help her with her grammar and accent, and she enrolled in speech classes. “I began to pay attention to my clothes,” she said. “Dressing appropriately for a role can help you play it better.” She began to wear tailored suits on the sidelines and got braces when she was nearly 30.

In a few short years, gone was the shy farm kid who always wore jeans and was self-conscious about her height. Summitt’s players affectionately referred to her as “Sarge” for her command and polish on the sidelines. Others called her “The Iron Lady” and marveled at her ability to consistently appear in a polished wardrobe reflecting the University of Tennessee’s signature colors. She even became known for a particular shade of blue: “Summitt Blue,” now recognized and worn by the University of Tennessee in athletic uniforms.

items.heading: Heading
items.paragraph: As someone who spent their life in the spotlight, Summitt’s personal brand was well-known. Your own brand may be less distinct, but it exists all the same. We’ll say it again: Your personal brand exists, whether you recognize that it does or not!
Scroll through to complete this element.

items.title: What Is Personal Brand?
items.description:
Personal brand incorporates a lot of things, but without overcomplicating it, there are four main parts:

●      Attitude

●      Image

●      Skills

●      Experience

items.title: Conclusion
items.description: When considering what your personal brand is, consider what you are known for specifically in each of these four main areas.

items.title: Attitude
items.description: What is the attitude you present in your role? What principles do you stand for? How do you communicate?

items.title: Image
items.description: What words would others use to describe you? What is your own signature look? What are you known for?

items.title: Skills
items.description: What expertise can you be counted on for? What things do you bring to the table? What is your superpower or special skill in your role?

items.title: Experience
items.description: Finally, what experiences make you unique? What events in your background are you known for that make up part of who you are?

items.heading: Does Personal Brand Matter if the Output Is Good?

items.paragraph: You may ask, “Does personal brand at work really matter if my output is good?” In a word, yes. In fact, it matters a whole lot more than you may think.

Personal brand affects consideration for promotions, specific tasks you’re given, what information you can be trusted with, whether you’re asked to present in a meeting, and whether your teammates want to work with you and follow you. After all, no one wants to work with (or follow) a successful jerk.

Your personal brand can have a profound impact on your personal life too, including your relationships and your overall success. Personal brand can sometimes even make up for a direct lack of skill or experience in certain areas.

items.title: Summary
items.description: Changing your personal brand takes time and effort. It may take weeks or months to see the results you want, but if you stay focused and committed, like Coach Summitt, you will eventually shape a winning, successful brand.

items.title: Identify your goals
items.description: What do you want to achieve with your personal brand? Do you want to be known for a particular skill or quality?

items.title: Develop a plan
items.description: Is there a gap between the image you’re projecting and the brand you would like to have?

items.title: Seek out opportunities
items.description: Look for opportunities to showcase your personal brand.
